title: The Nodrum — Exterior
subject: An ancient geometric ruins complex partially reclaimed by nature, with small-scale halfling modifications built onto much older, larger architecture
setting: A forested hillside or valley in a low-fantasy world. The facility is built into or emerges from the earth, suggesting something buried and only partially exposed.

architecture.ancient_layer: Massive stone blocks with precise geometric carvings — circles, triangles, intersecting lines. Tarnished bronze fixtures and mechanisms visible in the stonework. Verdigris patina on metal surfaces. The scale suggests this was built for something much larger than the current occupants.
architecture.modern_layer: Halfling-sized wooden doors, scaffolding, rope ladders, and small balconies bolted onto the ancient structure. Practical, clever, but clearly improvised against something monumental. Lanterns hang from brackets. A chimney has been added.

mood: Quiet unease beneath scholarly curiosity. A place where someone small and clever has made a home inside something vast and unknowable.
lighting: Late afternoon or early evening. Warm natural light from above, but pale amber light leaks from cracks and seams in the ancient stonework — suggesting active energy within.
color_palette: warm wood browns for halfling additions
composition: Slightly low angle, looking up at the entrance. The viewer is arriving — this is a first impression. The halfling-scale door should be visible but dwarfed by the ancient stonework surrounding it.
do_not_include: characters or figures in the scene
glowing magic runes on the exterior
